verdict: Late-cycle and expensive on rent/income fundamentals, but credit metrics remain healthy. The historical pattern for Indian metros is a multi-year time correction (flat prices), not a foreclosure-driven crash — the main downside trigger is an IT hiring shock, not lending.

indicators.name: Unsold inventory overhang
indicators.note: Rose from ~9 months (2024) as launches outpace absorption (~70k unsold units vs ~57k/yr sales pace). Cyclical rebalancing; NCR exceeded 60 months in 2017 for comparison.

indicators.name: Launch mix skew to luxury
indicators.note: New supply increasingly investor-oriented premium stock; end-user mid-market squeezed out — a classic late-cycle developer signal.

indicators.name: EMI-to-income (affordability)
indicators.note: Bengaluru remains below the lender stress threshold; affordability improved with ~125 bp of repo rate cuts since Feb 2025.

indicators.name: Housing-loan defaults (NPAs)
indicators.note: Bank gross NPAs at a 12-year low (~2.6%); mortgages are the cleanest retail book. Retail stress is concentrated in unsecured credit (≈52% of new retail NPAs, H1FY25), not housing. No public locality-level default data; SARFAESI e-auction counts are the best city-level distress proxy.

indicators.name: Asking vs registered price gap
indicators.note: Mid-market listings sit well above registry transaction averages (e.g. Chandra Layout ~₹7.8k asking vs ~₹5.6k registered) — listing-based indices, including this site, overstate clearing prices.

indicators.name: Registration volumes
indicators.note: Karnataka stamp-duty collections and Kaveri registration counts show transaction demand holding — real absorption, not just listings.
